newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: Taleban concede fall of Afghan town.
newsitem.headline: Taleban concede fall of Afghan town.

text.p: Afghanistan's Taleban government conceded on Monday it had lost the northern frontline town of Jabal os-Siraj and was fighting ousted government forces around Bagram airbase.

Acting deputy foreign minister Sher Mohammad Stanakzai told a news conference the Taleban were resisting forces of former government military chief Ahmad Shah Masood around Charikar, south of Jabal os-Siraj, and the nearby Bagram airbase, an hour's drive north of Kabul.
"Jabal os-Siraj at the moment is with them, but Bagram airbase is with Taleban and even our forces are ahead of Bagram airbase as well," Stanakzai said.
He said Taleban forces were holding some areas around Charikar, a town reliable sources said on Sunday had fallen to Masood's forces.
Stanakzai's comments were the first official admission that the Taleban had been pushed back from positions on its northern frontline.
He said fighting in these areas had taken place on Sunday, but added he did not have information about the situation on Monday.
